Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an
Flanking the sides of the porch are two stone piers topped with two Doric wooden columns supporting the wood roof with composite shingles.

files.title: File:Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an Douglas Co KS farmhouse south elevation.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption:
Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an
The stone house is an I-shape with a side-gable roof, and the south façade (primary façade) is symmetrical with a small wooden porch in the center framing the doorway with a one-over-one window on either side at both levels.

files.title: File:Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an Douglas Co KS farmhouse northeast corner looking southwest.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption:
Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an
Thomas McQuillian, traveling from Wisconsin, settled in Willow Springs in 1856, soon after the

Massachusetts Emigrant Aid Company came to Douglas County. Thomas was born in County Derry, Ireland, on April 22, 1817.

files.title: File:Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an Douglas Co KS farmhouse west elevation looking east.jpg
files.author: SharonPapierdreams
files.caption:
Kansas Homestead of Thomas McQuill(i)an
The west façade has two distinctive parts, the side-gable end of the stone structure and the wood-framed, two-story1900 addition extending from the center of the stone portion. The 1869 portion is symmetrical with the distinctive stacked stone chimney in the center.
